title: Approve a requirement basis before detailed design exists
goal: Decide whether the proposed requirement basis is sufficient for downstream design.
context: Requirement analysis supplies proposed changes or justified reuse, while Functions and ARs may be unfinished.
trigger: The author requests independent Requirement Review.
preconditions: The requested scope and relevant project authority are identifiable.

interaction.action: Supplies the RR basis, exact requirement and supporting analysis subjects, proposed disposition and acceptance criteria.
Assesses request fidelity, ownership, coverage, assessability and material uncertainty.
Records a scoped judgment and any findings against the exact basis.
Presents the judgment and its design-reliance limits.

expected_outcome: A justified independent judgment establishes or withholds the requirement basis for design without claiming design or implementation completeness.

alternatives.condition: Existing requirements fully cover the request.
alternatives.outcome: The review assesses the reuse conclusion without requiring artificial edits.

alternatives.condition: Required logical behavior and architectural allocations are not yet designed.
alternatives.outcome: A sufficient requirement basis may be accepted while the later design obligations remain explicit.

failures.condition: The author supplies their own judgment as independent review, or material requirements are ambiguous.
failures.outcome: The gate does not establish independent acceptance and exposes the missing basis or correction.

failures.condition: Material requirement subjects change after the assessment.
failures.outcome: Earlier approval retains its original meaning and is not silently applied to the revised basis.

sources.basis: User-selected requirement-first workflow and one mandatory whole-change Code Review gate. Proposed requirement analysis only; existing product contracts remain active until coordinated adoption. No new Function, AR, implementation or approval is inferred.

Document-based author assessment under the explicit Constitution exception confirms this Scenario as requirement-analysis knowledge. It is not independent review, executed product evidence or workflow activation.
